goalTextEn: Can introduce your teammates and describe their roles.
goalTextKr: 팀원을 소개하고 역할을 설명할 수 있다.

introduce.goalEn: Can introduce your teammates and describe their roles.
introduce.goalKr: 팀원을 소개하고 역할을 설명할 수 있다.
introduce.situationEn: A new employee has joined your team. Your manager asks you to introduce the team members. Tell the new person about everyone.
introduce.situationKr: 팀에 새 직원이 들어왔습니다. 상사가 팀원들을 소개해 달라고 합니다. 새 사람에게 모든 사람에 대해 알려주세요.

tutorNotes.text: "Today, you'll practice introducing other people — your teammates. Let's learn how to say who they are and what they do."
Read the lesson goal aloud. Ask the student to repeat.
"Is it clear?"
Read the situation. Check the student understands.
"Let's go to the next part."
Remind the student: Lessons 1-2 were about 'I'. Now it's about 'he/she/they'.

patterns.kr: 이쪽은 켄지입니다. 그는 우리의 경리 담당입니다.

patterns.en: We work together in the sales team.
He/She is in charge of customer support.

vocabulary.definition: a person who leads a team

pronunciation.instruction: Let's practice hearing the difference between /θ/ (th) and /s/.

tutorNotes.text: "Let's look at phrases for introducing other people."
Read each pattern aloud. Ask the student to repeat.
Explain 'This is' is used for introducing someone in person.
"Now let's learn some useful words."
Teach each vocabulary word. Ask the student to use it in a sentence.
For Japanese learners, 'colleague' is often confused with 'college'. Practice both.

understand.instruction: Fill in the blanks with the correct pattern. Then practice the pattern drills.
understand.instructionKr: 빈칸에 올바른 패턴을 넣으세요. 그런 다음 패턴 드릴을 연습하세요.

examples.en: This is Kenji. He is our accountant.
This is Maria. She is our new intern.
She works in the marketing department.
He works in the sales department.
She is in charge of customer support.
He is in charge of quality control.

tutorNotes.text: Ask the student to fill in the blanks, then practice the drills.
Ensure the student uses he/she correctly — practice if needed.

steps.title: Step 1 — Repeat the Introductions
steps.content:
1. This is Kenji. He is our accountant. He works in the finance department.
2. This is Maria. She is a sales assistant. She works in the sales department.
3. This is David. He is our IT manager. He is in charge of the company network.
4. This is Yuki. She is our designer. She works in the marketing department.

tutorNotes.text: Read each set of sentences. Ask the student to repeat.
Focus on smooth delivery — linking the sentences naturally.
Practice 'This is' — make sure 'th' is clear.

steps.title: Step 2 — Complete the Introduction
steps.instructionEn: Fill in the blanks to complete the introductions.
steps.content:
1. This is Naomi. She is our _______________. She works in the _______________ department.
2. This is Takeshi. He is a _______________. He is in charge of _______________.
3. This is Lisa. She is our _______________. She works in the _______________ department.
4. This is (your colleague). He/She is _______________. He/She works in _______________.

tutorNotes.text: For items 1-3, the student can use any reasonable job/department.
For item 4, the student uses a real colleague's information.
Encourage creativity. There's no single correct answer for 1-3.

steps.title: Step 3 — Team Introduction Dialogue
steps.instructionEn: Practice the dialogue with your tutor. You are introducing team members to a new employee.
steps.instructionKr: 선생님과 대화를 연습하세요. 신입사원에게 팀원들을 소개하고 있습니다.

dialogue.en: Hi! I'm the new employee. Can you tell me about the team?
dialogue.kr: 안녕하세요! 신입사원입니다. 팀에 대해 알려주실 수 있나요?

dialogue.en: Sure! This is Kenji. He is our accountant.
dialogue.kr: 물론이죠! 이쪽은 켄지입니다. 그는 경리 담당입니다.

dialogue.en: Nice to meet you, Kenji. And who is she?
This is Maria. She works in the sales department.
dialogue.kr: 이쪽은 마리아입니다. 그녀는 영업부에서 일하고 있습니다.

dialogue.en: That is David. He is our IT manager. He is in charge of the company network.
dialogue.kr: 저쪽은 데이비드입니다. 그는 IT 매니저이고, 회사 네트워크를 담당하고 있습니다.

dialogue.en: Your team is great! Do you all work together?
dialogue.kr: 좋은 팀이네요! 모두 함께 일하고 있나요?

dialogue.en: Yes, we work together in the Tokyo office.
dialogue.kr: 네, 도쿄 오피스에서 함께 일하고 있습니다.

tutorNotes.text: Practice the dialogue. Encourage the student to speak in full sentences.
After the first run, try it again without looking at the screen.
If the student is ready, add extra questions like 'What department does she work in?'

steps.title: Step 4 — Introduce Your Real Team
steps.instructionEn: Introduce 3 of your real colleagues or classmates to your tutor. Use the patterns you learned.
steps.instructionKr: 실제 동료나 반 친구 3명을 선생님에게 소개하세요. 배운 패턴을 사용하세요.
steps.content:
For each person, say:
- This is ___.
- He/She is a/an ___.
- He/She works in the ___ department.
- He/She is in charge of ___.

tutorNotes.text: "Now, introduce 3 of your real colleagues to me. Pretend I'm new at your company!"
Let the student speak freely. Help if they get stuck.
After each introduction, ask a follow-up question: 'What department?' or 'Is he/she nice?'
If the student doesn't have colleagues, they can introduce friends or family members.

challenge.scenarioEn: You are at a company event. A client asks you to introduce your team. Introduce at least 4 people with their names, roles, and departments.
challenge.scenarioKr: 회사 행사에 있습니다. 고객이 팀 소개를 요청했습니다. 최소 4명의 이름, 역할, 부서를 소개하세요.

guideQuestions.text: Who is the first person? What is their role?
Who works in the sales department?
Who is in charge of the biggest project?
Introduce someone you work closely with.
Ask the client to introduce themselves too!

tutorNotes.text: "Challenge time! I'm a client visiting your company. Please introduce your team to me."
Play the client. React naturally: 'Oh, nice to meet them!' 'What does she do?'
The student should introduce at least 4 people.
If the student introduces 4+ people smoothly with 'This is / He works in / She is in charge of', they've achieved the goal.

discussion.instructionEn: Choose one category, then answer the questions.

categories.title: YOUR TEAM
questions: How many people are on your team?
Who has worked there the longest?

categories.title: YOUR MANAGER
questions: What is he/she in charge of?

categories.title: IDEAL COLLEAGUES
questions: Do you prefer working alone or in a team?
What's the best thing about your team?

tutorNotes.text: "Let's have a discussion about your team."
Ask the student to choose a category.
Encourage the student to use today's patterns in their answers.

feedback.goalReviewEn: Can introduce your teammates and describe their roles.

"Were you able to achieve today's lesson goal?"
Fill in and send the feedback template.
